content: What are the chances your stake is worth close to double what you personally invested? For much of its existence, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSM -1.67%), or TSMC, has been one of the more underappreciated companies in the tech world. We don't interact with its products or services, but as the world's largest semiconductor foundry, it makes chips for virtually all the electronics we use every day. TSMC has been around for nearly four decades, but the recent AI boom has brought it into the spotlight. Over the past three years, its stock is up 325%, and it's now the world's sixth-most-valuable public company. TSMC has strong momentum, up 35% this year, but what could $500 monthly investments in the stock look like over the nearly three years leading into 2030? Let's take a look. For illustration, let's assume TSMC finishes this year flat from its current price, giving you three full years of investing from 2027 to 2030. Values rounded to the nearest dollar. The exact percentages and values will inevitably fluctuate because each $500 monthly investment compounds differently, but they roughly reflect what you can expect under various growth environments. Which is more likely? TSMC has been trading on the market since October 1997 (on the New York Stock Exchange), but most of its all-time gains have come in the past three years, during which it has averaged nearly 60% annual returns. I don't see it continuing at that pace over the next three years, but I believe the 25% AI boom scenario is very doable, and investors could see their stake grow above $35,000. Many investors would agree that valuations have grown out of control during the current AI mania. That could cause some stock sell-offs over the next few years, but from a business standpoint, the data center and AI infrastructure build-out isn't ending for TSMC anytime soon. TSMC's business is well positioned for the next few years because it's the go-to for virtually all advanced AI chip manufacturing needs. It doesn't matter whether AMD catches up to Nvidia's GPU dominance, whether the hyperscalers (Amazon, Microsoft, Alphabet, and Meta Platforms) begin designing their own chips, or whether Broadcom has a stronghold on AI accelerators. TSMC is who'll bring their chip designs to life. Being the only game in town has given TSMC unprecedented pricing power, which it has used to expand margins and drive record profits. In the past three years, its revenue has jumped 138% ($46.7 billion in the third quarter), while its net income has jumped 219%. TSMC's high-performance computing segment (which includes its advanced AI chips) accounted for 68% of its revenue last quarter, so there's no doubt an AI-specific slowdown would affect its growth rate. However, TSMC's management has remained confident about sustainable demand, citing multiyear agreements and the rise of agentic AI, which requires more compute and, therefore, more advanced chips that only TSMC can manufacture at scale. TSMC projects 2026 revenue to be 44% higher than 2025, putting it around $176 billion. At its size, revenue growth rates will eventually slow, but I don't see it dropping below 25% annually before 2030. One thing to always remember is that nobody can predict how a stock will perform. Even if TSMC keeps posting impressive results (which I think it will), that doesn't necessarily mean its stock will follow suit. The market can sometimes be irrational. That said, TSMC is a great investment option well beyond the next three years. Even if the stock hits a rough patch, the company's industry dominance and expertise give it one of the largest competitive moats in the tech world. Semiconductor manufacturing will only become more important over time. So regardless of how the current AI arms race plays out, TSMC stands to gain a lot. title: TSM Stock: TSMC Confirms Employee Data Leak as Seller Seeks 3 Bitcoin for the Records - FinanceFeeds
content: TSMC confirmed on Thursday that data belonging to some current and former employees was posted on an external website without authorization. The company said so in a statement filed with the SEC, and sellers on two underground forums are asking 3 Bitcoin for the records, worth about $220,000 at Thursday’s price of $73,444. TSM stock closed Wednesday at $413.35, up 4.25%, after October revenue of NT$586.89 billion rose 59.7% year over year. TSM stock was quoted at $393.11 in Thursday’s premarket, down 4.90%, alongside a broad semiconductor selloff. The filing, signed by chief financial officer Wendell Huang, says the company has “found no evidence that TSMC’s systems have been compromised.” It adds that the exposed information “has been verified to match data stored in the system services of a cloud service provider.” TSMC says the leaked data is unrelated to its operations or its customers, and that it is notifying affected personnel. It is working with the cloud vendor, investigating authorities and a third-party cybersecurity firm. The company has not named the provider or said how the records left it. Form 6-K is the route that puts the disclosure in front of holders of TSM stock. Sellers on DarkForums and BreachForums claim roughly 46,000 records totaling 6.9GB and have threatened to publish everything if nobody buys within a week, according to Business Next. The asking price converts to about NT$7.4 million by local media calculation, and Taiwan News carried the confirmation the same day. A sample file named tsmc.txt holds 499 entries with 19 fields each. The fields cover name, date of birth, job title, nationality, national ID number, home address, mobile number, email, bank information and the phone number and address of an emergency contact. Those fields come from the sellers rather than from TSMC, which has confirmed the leak without specifying what it contained. If the sample is authentic, the exposure reaches relatives listed as emergency contacts who never worked at the company, which widens the affected population well past the headcount behind TSM stock. TSMC’s filing places the data inside a cloud vendor’s systems and outside its own, so the financial exposure behind TSM stock is a liability question about outsourced processing rather than a breach of the fabs or customer designs. Taiwan has logged five disclosed incidents in five weeks, and three of them point at an outside system. The 104 Job Bank said about 120,000 resumes were read without authorization on 6 October. 91APP reported exposure of order data for 1,329 brands and roughly 4.79 million consumers on 16 October, after an unpatched flaw in the third-party tool Appsmith. E.Sun Bank disclosed 418 accounts drained of NT$41.76 million on 3 November through an external supplier’s new banking system, and ezTravel put more than 690,000 people at risk on 9 November. TSMC is the fifth, and the smallest by headcount apart from the bank, which is why the sequence matters more to TSM stock than the count does. The same shape repeats outside Taiwan, and Coinbase denied a direct breach while confirming customer information was exposed through an analytics vendor on 3 November. DriveWealth blamed a social engineering campaign for a Revolut customer data breach, and Gnosis Pay disclosed its own customer breach on 7 November. Thursday’s decline in TSM stock arrived with Nvidia down 6.03% premarket after the Wall Street Journal reported that its board is preparing to remove Jensen Huang. Micron, Arm and Marvell had all closed higher on Wednesday, and the whole complex reversed overnight, which puts the move on the Nvidia story rather than on the leak. TSM stock is up 32.49% this year and down 8.86% over a month, on TradingView data, with a market capitalization of $1.89 trillion and a trailing price to earnings ratio of 25.52. The January to October revenue total reached NT$4,485.62 billion, up 43.3%, which is the trajectory that took TSM stock to $430 after the Q3 print. Fourth-quarter results are due around 21 January, which gives the investigation two months to produce a named vendor before management next faces questions. Article 4 of Taiwan’s Personal Data Protection Act treats a contractor that collects, processes or uses personal data on a company’s behalf as the commissioning agency. Outsourcing the processing does not transfer the obligation, so whether TSMC carries liability depends on whether either party breached the act and whether damage followed. How the two split it depends on the investigation and their contract. Article 29 puts the burden on a non-government body to prove it acted without intent or negligence. Where a victim cannot establish actual losses, courts may award NT$500 to NT$20,000 per person per incident, with a NT$200 million cap across a single event. TSMC has announced no compensation plan, and Article 34 allows qualifying public interest organizations to bring group actions, which is the route that would put a number on the TSM stock exposure. title: AI Sell-Off: Buy ANET, TSM & MU to Make Up for NVIDIA Losses - TradingView
content: The artificial intelligence (AI) trade is facing one of its toughest tests yet. After driving Wall Street's rally for much of 2026, technology and semiconductor stocks have come under intense selling pressure as investors question lofty valuations, the sustainability of hyperscaler capital expenditures and the time required to monetize massive AI investments. Rising inflation, higher Treasury yields and uncertainty surrounding data-center construction have added to the pressure. The weakness is also evident in AI-focused ETFs. Over the past 30 days, the Global X Artificial Intelligence & Technology ETF (AIQ) has declined 11.4%, while the iShares Future AI & Tech ETF (ARTY) has plunged 17.1%, entering correction territory. ARTY's steeper decline indicates the extent of selling pressure across companies positioned to benefit from future AI adoption. The Nov. 5 sell-off was particularly severe. The iShares Semiconductor ETF SOXX plunged 12.1%. The pressure escalated on Nov. 8 following a corporate governance controversy involving NVIDIA NVDA. NVIDIA shares fell 4.27% on Nov. 9 as concerns over leadership continuity, board oversight and potential national-security implications weighed on investor sentiment. The sell-off deepened on Nov. 10, with NVIDIA losing another 6.5% and the Nasdaq Composite declining 1%. Broader concerns over AI infrastructure spending, complications surrounding a major Ohio data-center project and hotter-than-expected inflation further undermined technology stocks. However, does this correction signal the end of the AI investment opportunity, or is it creating an attractive entry point in fundamentally strong companies? Let's find out. Here, we have picked three AI stocks — Arista Networks ANET, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company TSM or TSMC and Micron Technology MU — all carrying favorable Zacks Rank and having strong fundamentals, making them attractive alternatives to NVIDIA for investors seeking AI exposure beyond the market leader amid the current volatility. Why Quality AI Stocks Beyond NVIDIA Are Attractive Now Despite the correction, long-term AI infrastructure demand remains strong. According to IDC's Nov. 6 report, global AI infrastructure spending reached $121.4 billion in the second quarter, up 53.3% year over year. IDC raised its 2026 spending forecast to $521 billion from $497 billion previously and expects the market to reach $1.17 trillion by 2029. Notably, non-accelerated, CPU-based infrastructure spending grew 61.1%, outpacing the 52.2% growth in accelerated systems, highlighting expanding investment opportunities beyond GPU suppliers. Meanwhile, J.P. Morgan projected AI capital expenditure of approximately $900 billion in 2026, although financing, electricity availability and semiconductor supply remain constraints. This spending creates opportunities beyond NVIDIA across AI networking, advanced semiconductor manufacturing, high-bandwidth memory and computing processors. Investors should focus on companies translating AI demand into measurable revenue growth and stronger earnings rather than speculative AI exposure. Arista: It is benefiting from increasing demand for high-speed Ethernet networking in AI data centers. Its third-quarter 2026 revenues surged 58.5% year over year, while non-GAAP EPS increased to $1.20 from 77 cents a year earlier. Non-GAAP operating margin reached 49.1%. Management expects fourth-quarter revenues of $3.9-$4 billion. ANET's networking exposure makes it an attractive means to participate in AI infrastructure expansion beyond chip manufacturing. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for 2026 earnings indicates growth of 45.6% on current-year sales growth of 47.9%. TSMC offers exposure to AI demand across multiple chip designers, rather than relying on a single GPU manufacturer. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for 2026 earnings suggests 63.9% growth, while sales are expected to increase 40.9%. Over the past seven days, 2026 earnings estimates for TSM have been revised upward by 2.3% to $17.46 per share. The stock sports a Zacks Rank #1. The company reported strong fiscal fourth quarter 2026 revenues of $54.23 billion, compared with $11.32 billion a year earlier. Micron has also commenced high-volume shipments of HBM4.
